newsitem.title: USA: AccuStaff buys Career Horizons for $1 billion.
newsitem.headline: AccuStaff buys Career Horizons for $1 billion.

text.p: AccuStaff Inc. has signed a definitive agreement to acquire Career Horizons Inc. in a deal valued at $1 billion, creating the nation's fourth-largest employment company, they said Monday.

The new company, operating as AccuStaff Inc., will provide staffing, consulting and outsourcing services. It will have more than 750 offices in 43 states and annual revenues of more than $1.3 billion, climbing to above $1.7 billion in 1997.
Career's stock leaped $5 to $36.875 on the New York Stock Exchange after the announcement. AccuStaff fell $2 to $26 on Nasdaq.

"Both AccuStaff and Career Horizons have been major consolidators in the industry and this transaction accelerates that trend, creating an even stronger platform for growth and additional acquisitions," said Derek Dewan, AccuStaff's chairman, president and CEO.
"Our combined cash position, together with credit facilities, gives us the liquidity to make strategic and even larger acquisitions."

Since its initial public offering in August 1994, Jacksonville, Fla.-based AccuStaff has completed 33 acquisitions in the staffing industry. Its 1996 revenues were projected to reach $772 million prior to the latest merger.

Woodbury, N.Y.-based Career Horizons provides temporary personnel for clerical, commercial, hospital and other healthcare functions, as well as information technology. Its revenues for 1995 were $385 million and are projected to reach about $613 million in 1996. It has 574 offices in 43 states.

Under the agreement, AccuStaff will offer about 1.53 shares of its stock for Career Horizons' shares in a tax-free pooling of interests. The exchange ratio is subject to adjustment, and will range from 1.2444 to 1.8006.
Based on AccuStaff's $28-per-share closing price as of Friday, the deal is valued at about $1 billion, the companies said in a statement.
The deal, which has been unanimously approved by the both companies' boards, is expected to close during the fourth quarter.

"We expect the merger to be accretive to AccuStaff's earnings for the first full year of combined operations and we believe it will also add significant long-term value to our shareholders," Dewan said.

Dewan will remain as chairman, president and chief executive of AccuStaff following the merger. Career Horizon's president and chief executive, Walter Macauley, will join AccuStaff's board of directors as vice chairman.
